mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals weak labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, causing a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signal a stagflationary environment that erodes corporate margins and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both UNRATE > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (UNRATE * CPIAUCSL) as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (defined by quarterly GDP growth above 2.0% and monthly industrial production growth above 0.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to overvaluation and anticipation of monetary tightening, resulting in a 20-day return decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% (q/q) and INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% (m/m), or the Rank IC for the regime condition as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong manufacturing activity and corporate capacity utilization, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% (m/m), or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) reading above 1500 thousand units signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST exceeds 1500, or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 3.5%) and high consumer spending (RSAFS > 700,000 million dollars) signal an accommodative monetary policy combined with strong demand, which fuels equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.5% and RSAFS > 700000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (FEDFUNDS * RSAFS) as a predictor of 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of accelerating labor market tightness (measured by a decline in UNRATE below 4.0% and a rise in PAYEMS above 150,000 thousand persons), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns due to rising corporate hiring and wage growth, leading to a 20-day return increase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 150000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (UNRATE * PAYEMS) as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
